established.method: Semantic revert rather than file revert: resolveContactUrl is a NEW exported symbol, so reverting src/lib/contactUrl.ts deletes the symbol the test imports and the reverted world cannot compile (the documented UNPROVABLE case). Instead I collapsed the resolver body to the hardcoded 'return FALLBACK_CONTACT_URL' that the plan explicitly rejected — the pre-change behaviour expressed in the post-change interface — ran refresh-tests --changed, then restored the real body from a scratchpad copy and re-ran.
established.evidence: Faulted: {failed:3, passed:6, total:9}. The three that flipped red are exactly the nav-derivation assertions: 'follows a Contact item that has been moved to a different url', 'prefers the label match over a url match when the nav contains both', and 'matches the label case-insensitively'. Restored: {failed:0, passed:9}. The six that stayed green are fallback/default-nav survival guards that legitimately hold under both worlds.
